svg.text: PART 5: ESP32-CAM LINK TO THE STM32 (UART)
Test setup for step 3. Only the laptop USB is needed: the Nucleo 5V pin feeds the top + rail (5 V).
USB cable to the laptop (power and code)
outside the board, camera facing the bowl,
joined with 4 female to male wires
The pin order can look reversed on your board:
match every wire by its printed name
Other row: U0T, U0R and IO0 stay free,
stops restarts on WiFi current peaks
1 kΩ in the STM32 TX line (columns 29 to 32):
protects both pins, does not slow the messages
Column map of the whole feeder:
5 V: Nucleo 5V to the top + rail; ESP32-CAM 5V
ESP32-CAM IO15 (TX) to Nucleo D21 · PC7 (RX)
Nucleo D16 · PC6 (TX), 1 kΩ, ESP32-CAM IO14 (RX)
Wires at the ESP32-CAM: 5V, GND, IO15, IO14,
all on the same pin row
Both boards use 3.3 V signals: no divider
1000 µF on the rails: no restarts on WiFi peaks
Test program: load it first with the DevKit
1. Wire everything with the USB unplugged.
3. Keep the ESP32-CAM microSD slot empty.
4. Short 5V and GND wires if you have them.
5. Restarts again and again: power problem.
6. Check every Nucleo pin label before plugging.
Kibbly hardware · circuit 5 of the circuits by part · wires E1 to E9 in hardware/04_wiring_list.md section 5, rails R1, R3 and R4 in section 4B
